reasons: Correctly identifies § 4(c) as the operative licence grant running to us and flags the three preferred-position gaps (no affiliates/contractors, silent on irrevocability, silent on transfer against the § 10 anti-assignment bar) — a genuine deviation, not a walk-away.

Redline is directionally correct for the customer: adds 'and its affiliates', 'irrevocable', a sublicence/exercise right for contractors acting on our behalf, and successor transferability, while preserving the existing royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual sublicensable grant and the original operative verbs.
Insertions are grammatically clean and surgical; the 0.565 changed-character ratio reflects the three distinct elements the rule requires rather than an unnecessary rewrite of the clause.

Comment is accurate, uses the [Playbook] prefix and first-person plural, states what changed and the playbook basis, and offers the fallback (affiliates on written notice, M&A successor transfer) without lecturing.
Minor, non-blocking: 'affiliates' is lowercase and the agreement may not define the term; if an 'Affiliate' definition exists elsewhere, capitalising it would tighten the edit.
